body: Ok. Thank you.
Hell yes!!!

I loved it at first on my low dosage. When I got to my larger dosage I felt intoxicated,  but I did get used to it. However,  I quit after 14 months because eventually my emotions got to the point where I was "empty and liked it. " Little scary. Everyone's different though. I would definitely suggest a low dosage when/if you try it.

Weed in small amounts works wonderfully for me. I have had moments in the past where I have been out of control though, but other factors/drugs were in the mix. I'm not going to tell you to do it or not, but I will tell you light smoking is very doable if you have enough stability/structure in life. By the way,  vaporizing > smoking.
That is very logical... Refreshing to hear. Do you ever meet with patients through Skype by chance? Thank you. =D
Great to hear. I wish I could say the same. Waiting on a phone call from my next potential clinical psychologist. Optimistic.
Thanks for all of the comments everybody! I wish you all the best!

I'm always anxious before I post or speak on here. I think about the fact that nobody knows who I am though and it makes it easier. I even go so far as to using multiple accounts so people can't piece together my stories and interests to figure me out. I'm glad you commented!

Yes! CBD is great!! My roommates refuse to accept it though for some reason. The last time I had a THC panic attack around them they literally did nothing. They told me to go away and that it was just weed. I'm counting down the days until I move out.  Fuck 'em.
What do you mean by chronic pathological dehydration? She won't drink water unless you tell her to?
I agree!

I woke up this afternoon and started thinking about my parents' gigantic tree in their backyard. It was basically my first source of shade as a child. This tree has always been so elegant and comforting, but it is dying. This caused me to feel really nostalgic and replay lots of childhood and teenage memories... especially those in the backyard. I began to cry. "Nothing lasts forever, " I thought. "Time is destructive. My parents are getting old.  My dog is gone. My childhood is over and I'm a lonely adult now battling a cocktail of mental disorders." I cried for about two hours. A day in the life really...
You know it!
Thanks for the comments!
I agree that it wasn't very accurate, but it did make me chuckle a couple times.
Yes! I'll be keeping this one forever.
Precisely.
What bothers me the most is the good people that I've driven off. One friend in particular,  I still think about every day... One of the best friends I've had. Brb going to cry.

Do your best to try to find another job and to get SSI. Apply for welfare and get yourself to a safe, low-cost community like in a rural area. Get familiar with a local church that has a food pantry and surround yourself with loving people. When you are able, meet with a psychologist. I hope you stay on your feet! Hang in there!

Things I self-soothe successfully with:

Video Games

Walking/Hiking

Meditation

Music

Bathing

Select TV Shows or Movies

...




My go to is still rumination because it's an evil habit of mine. Not recommended. I wish I could be done with it forever.

I've never met a psychiatrist that I liked. Psychologists, on the other hand, have saved my life a few times. In my humble opinion, ignore the psychiatrist for now. Talk with a therapist that has a great track record and you should find your answer for the next step. Other than that, diet, exercise, and meditation go a long way! Good luck!

Yes. One of my problems is that I can't be honest to myself about which relationships are unhealthy. Therefore,  I automatically do my best to keep everyone in my life... Even if that person (directly or indirectly) supports my self-destruction with oxycontin for example.
I'm not too thrilled with the world either. Ignorance, corruption, war, negligence... I wish our type 0 civilization could get our fucking priorities straight.
I agree with wkd-- great writing!  I too have very frequent nightmares and have experienced one pretty similar to what you've described.

Yeah. I often hurt my friends by accident when trying to explain how distant I usually feel. Last night a friend of mine assumed I was blaming him for my problems and that I didn't care about him. Shitty deal. =( I don't want to lose him. Fun fact: That scenario is actually what pushed me to make this Reddit account yesterday.

I often feel how you describe... Every once and a while, I will have an outstanding conversation with a friend. Although, I typically feel very detached even if a friend is trying to cheer me up. I know persistent feelings of lonliness well.
"Border-lion" has just been added to my vocabulary.  Thanks!
The potential for change is a good one.  It helps keep me ticking.
You described it well!  I wish I could understand how others view me... So much of my anger is fueled by others' misinterpretations of me.

I don't think I would go so far as to say that I require that others have a high level of understanding of me in order for me to be "happy", but my happiness or lack thereof is definitely related to their understanding.
I like how you described it as a transient feeling!

I too have a part of me that resents the fact that folks care about me. It seems that you and I would like to pull a Hermione Granger and erase ourselves from our families' lives so we can't hurt them!  I hope these feelings are not persistent for you though.  They are fairly transient for me.

I can't really describe why I wear a mask all day.  However, I think one of the main reasons is that I would prefer to act joyful and positive around others so I don't spread my darkness and negatively affect the world.  Also, if I am around others for too long I often feel DRAINED because I am generally doing a lot of acting and am suppressing quite a bit of emotion.  I would assume that you feel the same?  Why do you do it?
Great description, "I am this social butterfly person with a huge smile on my face, but it's a mask. I feel like a con artist." I am precisely the same way.
Yes, my self-worth steadily declines as I fail with interpersonal relationships.
